_note: Custom policy schema for the Hermes engineering swarm v2. This is NOT Hermes configuration; do not paste into ~/.hermes. Every dollar and minute value is a configurable starting value, not a price estimate or spending authorization. Fields named _confirm must be checked against the provider's current API reference before a smoke run.

E1.name: Small
E1.description: One module, reproducible, roughly under 50 changed lines, under an hour.

E2.name: Medium
E2.description: Several files, needs independent test design, up to a day.

E3.name: Large
E3.description: Cross-module or cross-service, concurrency, debugging without a clear cause, multi-day.

E4.name: Foundational
E4.description: Architecture, novel design, major ambiguity; must be decomposed before implementation.
E4.ceiling_scope: plan; items carry their own ceilings; a separate project ceiling applies

hermes._scope: plan node; items use their own effort level

effort_heuristics._note: Stage-1 rules used by router.py. Signals come from the task JSON. Requester may raise effort, never lower it.

T2.name: Bug fix, reproducible
examples: wrong total on a report page

T4.name: Tests & fixtures
examples: fixtures for the recruiter pipeline app

T13.name: Architecture & design decision
examples: data model for a new product

matrix._grammar: Cell = <family>[+<modifiers>] | ->Tn[|Tm] (re-route to that task type at the same effort; alternatives chosen by signal) | ->reroute (misdescribed request; router returns reroute_required) | ^E1 (raise effort to E1 and look up again). Flag effects (flag_effects) add G and H on top of any cell.

_notes.T12.E0-E2: +H arrives through the prod flag (flag_effects), which is what '(+H if prod)' in the spec means.
_notes.T13.E3: R4 plan head only: the premium judge writes the ADR and decomposition; no implementation in this item.
_notes.T8: +G arrives through the payments, pii or secrets flag when derived from paths.

P.name: Reproduce first
P.on_failure: raise effort one level; if no reproduction within ceiling, stop with evidence

V.name: Eval replay
V.requires: pilot and holdout replay with non-regression on acceptance, cost per accepted item, p95 lead time

route_templates._note: Live nodes per family. Modifiers add or replace nodes. The item subgraph is TD -> RV, IM -> RV -> CK; families switch TD and RV on or off.

R1.name: Light
R1.contract: short, implementer tier, checked by reviewer (P when +G)

R4.name: Planned
R4.contract: P writes milestone contract and decomposition

node_tiers._note: Tier per node. 'by_effort:<field>' reads the effort level. Deterministic nodes have no model.

t1_mechanical: no behavioral change (AST-level diff, or F-tier reviewer for R1)
t2_bug_repro: reproduction test red on base revision, green on candidate
targeted tests for the touched module
regression suite for the touched package
t3_bug_no_repro: produce a reproduction first (failing test or scripted repro); if none within the +P ceiling, stop with evidence
root-cause statement anchored to file and revision
t4_tests: new tests fail when the covered behavior is deliberately broken (mutation spot-check, >=1 assertion per test file)
tests assert on contract, not implementation details
t5_backend: contract tests for every changed interface
consumers of changed interfaces enumerated and updated or shown unaffected
independent test design from the contract
t6_frontend: real browser run of acceptance scenarios
screenshots at contract viewports compared to the contract by a vision-capable F/M model
snapshot tests alone are not evidence
t7_data_schema: dry run against a snapshot or copy
row counts and checksums reconciled before and after
seeds and backfills idempotent and scoped by explicit filters
t8_integration: fixture-payload replay in a sandbox or test account
idempotency proven: same event twice -> one effect
external API contract pinned with primary documentation link and retrieval date
secrets only via environment or broker
t9_refactor: existing tests pass unchanged (compile-level fallout only, confirmed by reviewer)
characterization tests added first where coverage is thin
public interfaces unchanged unless the contract says so
t10_research: evidence bundle: sources with URL, retrieval date, snippet
each claim tagged PASS / FAIL / NOT YET PROVEN
t11_security: no secret value enters model context
threat sketch for the changed surface
+H before rotation or any production change
t12_infra: plan or dry run reviewed (preview deployment, --dry-run, plan output)
readback of live state matches intent
rollback path executed at least once outside production for E2+
t13_architecture: ADR: decision, <=2 alternatives, interface/invariant contract, acceptance tests, rollback conditions
decomposition into items that each land in a matrix cell
t14_agent_policy: eval replay on pilot and holdout: no regression in acceptance rate, cost per accepted item, lead time

F2.name: Contract defect
examples: test designer and reviewer disagree on intent

decomposition_rules.D2: Concurrent items own disjoint files. Shared collision points (schemas, lockfiles, migrations, routing tables, generated clients) become their own items, serialized on the critical path.
decomposition_rules.D3: Every item has a testable acceptance criterion inherited from the milestone contract.
decomposition_rules.D4: Target E1-E2 per item. An item that cannot be brought under E3 is a T13 question, not an item.
decomposition_rules.D5: Items are similar in size: the longest is at most twice the median.
decomposition_rules.D6: Items under a +G parent carry contract.inherited_gate_ref; diverging assumptions need a new gate. Fragmenting work to evade the gate is a logged policy violation.

gate_reserve_model._note: Gate reserve = max(static gate_reserve_usd, computed). Computed = 2 premium calls at the expected context for the effort level, times safety_factor.

modes._note: Operating modes (SPEC §0): RIGOR levels, not model rosters. A mode may only raise rigor, width, budget/time ceilings or gates when the task type/impact flags require it; it never removes a mandatory recipe, premium gate, human interrupt, secret rule, idempotency rule or verification requirement. Model selection is fully decoupled from the mode: every tier is filled from the tier registry and dispatched on the model's own provider account. User-selected mode is a floor, not a ceiling (router may raise, never lower). Safety flags win over mode (rule 6).

easy.name: Easy
easy.use_when: Routine team workflows, cron jobs, simple setup, and tasks where the safe default is obvious.
easy.override_behavior: Use the least expensive verified route; prefer human-readable schedules, default delivery, narrow prompts, one owner, and no optional advanced knobs. Route E0-E1 work through R0/R1 unless task type/flags require more.
easy.minimum_proof: Artifact exists; relevant check/readback passes; cron/job/profile/skill loads successfully when applicable.

medium.name: Medium
medium.use_when: Normal product/engineering changes where several files or an external contract may be involved.
medium.override_behavior: Default to the matrix as written. Use independent test design and cross-family review for E2. Cap parallelism at disjoint owned-file sets, default width 4.
medium.minimum_proof: Contract plus targeted or independent tests; reviewer sees diff/source, not the implementer report; verification recipe passes on exact revision.

hard.name: Hard
hard.use_when: Cross-module, high-risk, ambiguous, production-adjacent, or failure-prone work.
hard.override_behavior: Raise effort one level when uncertainty is material; require explicit contract, stronger reviewer, evidence bundle when useful, and stricter time/spend checkpoints. Use R3 or R4 when E3+ or when decomposition reduces risk.
hard.minimum_proof: Integration/failure-injection checks where relevant; blocking findings resolved; state/event log records attempts, failures, gates, and exact revision.

expert.name: Expert
expert.use_when: Foundational architecture, security/data/schema, policy/routing changes, irreversible external writes, or anything the operator flags as expert.
expert.override_behavior: Treat as T13/T14 or critical row as appropriate. Use premium judge for contract/acceptance where flags or matrix require +G; use human interrupt +H before irreversible actions. Decompose into E1-E2 bounded items under one approved milestone contract.
expert.minimum_proof: Premium/human gates satisfied when required; holdout/eval replay for policy changes; readback/proof from external systems; ledger and final artifact reconcile.
